final_message:
Fix is in and verified; the full suite passes, including the new test.

The bug was in `record_failure` in `billing/dunning.py`. When retries ran out and the subscription was already canceled (or missing), it called `mark_uncollectible(ctx, invoice["final_action"])`. That passed a non-existent invoice key, which raised the `KeyError`, instead of the invoice id. I changed it to `invoice["id"]`, which matches the other `mark_uncollectible` call in the same function.

I also added your reproducing test as `tests/test_dunning_cancel.py`, and wrote `answer.json` with `{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "record_failure"}`.

steps.command:
sed -i 's/mark_uncollectible(ctx, invoice\["final_action"\])/mark_uncollectible(ctx, invoice["id"])/' billing/dunning.py && echo '{"file": "dunning.py", "function": "record_failure"}' > answer.json && cat >> tests/test_dunning_cancel.py <<'EOF'


def test_retries_exhausted_after_cancel_marks_uncollectible():
    from conftest import World

    w = World({"retry_offsets_days": [1], "final_action": "mark_unpaid"})
    cus = w.customer(last4="0002")
    sub = w.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(w.monthly["id"], 1)])
    w.engine.cancel(sub["id"], at_period_end=False)
    w.advance_days(1)
    [inv] = w.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert sub["status"] == "canceled"
    assert inv["status"] == "uncollectible"
EOF
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

cat >> tests/test_dunning_cancel.py <<'EOF'
